title: ci: add provenance bundles + staged release manifest pipeline for private-installer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: For Private deployments we need cryptographically verifiable release bundles (artifacts, SBOMs, attestations) and a deterministic, staged manifest that operators can consume for air-gapped or VPC installs. This PR wires a CI pipeline that builds release artifacts for the private-installer chart and associated Terraform modules, produces SLSA-style provenance attestations, signs artifacts with cosign (KMS-backed keys), uploads signed bundles to a staging bucket, and emits a chained release manifest that references digested artifacts and attestation records.

What changed (summary):
- New GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/release/provenance-manifest.yml that orchestrates build -> sbom -> attest -> sign -> stage -> manifest steps.
- Artifact builders: added scripts/packaging/build_private_bundle.sh that produces tar.gz bundles containing Helm chart, rendered kustomize overlays, module zip, and SBOM JSON.
- Signing: integrates cosign via k8s-secrets-backed KMS path (uses ephemeral signing key rotation step for CI). Cosign signatures and bundle attestations are uploaded alongside artifacts.
- Manifest generator: tools/release/manifest-assembler.go produces a 3-tier manifest (staged.json -> candidate.json -> release.json) with content-addressed references and provenance links. The pipeline stages the candidate manifest to a protected GCS bucket and only promotes to release.json after successful integration smoke-tests.
- Terraform tagging: CI now tags terraform modules with module semantic versions and updates private-installer/terraform/versions.tf on release.
- Helm guardrails: CI performs chart lint + policy (conftest) checks and records policy attestations in the manifest.
- Upgrade/rollback tooling: adds tools/release/rollback-helper.sh which can validate manifests and perform an automated rollback plan for in-cluster private deployments (uses chart and module digests to revert).

Checklist: 
- [x] Build artifacts for private-installer chart and terraform modules
- [x] Generate SBOMs (Syft) and attach to bundle
- [x] Produce SLSA-style provenance attestations for build steps
- [x] Sign artifacts with cosign (CI KMS key) and upload to staging
- [x] Produce chained manifests and store candidate in staging bucket
- [x] Run smoke/integration tests against candidate manifest in ephemeral VPC
- [x] Promote to release manifest on successful smoke tests

Operational notes:
- Signing key: CI uses the project KMS key; a rotation helper is included at scripts/ops/rotate_ci_signing_key.sh. For enterprise private customers we support uploading your own public key and verifying signatures locally (docs updated).
- Staging bucket layout: gs://redwood-private-releases/staging/{sha}/artifacts/..., manifests in gs://redwood-private-releases/manifests/candidate/{sha}.json and manifests/canonical/release-{semver}.json after promotion.
- Rollback: rollback-helper.sh inspects the release manifest and applies the previous release manifest via helmfile/apply or terraform apply -target, optionally running a pre-check suite. See NOTES_UPGRADE_ROLLBACK in the PR diff for commands.

Related: linear ENG-2418 (private-installer release automation), ENG-2560 (artifact signing & attestations).

notes_on_upgrade_rollback: Upgrade path: operators consume release.json and run release/upgrade.sh which applies terraform module tags, runs helmfile --file=release.json sync. For canary upgrades the pipeline produces a candidate manifest that targets a canary namespace; operators should run canary verification (integration-smoke) before promote. Rollback path: run tools/release/rollback-helper.sh --manifest=previous-release.json --kubeconfig=<path> --apply (or --dry-run). Rollback helper validates digest signatures, checks SBOM differences, and provides a plan via --plan output. In air-gapped installs, fetch signed bundle and verify cosign signatures locally with 'cosign verify-blob --signature <sig> <artifact>' using the provided public key.
